name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-ptc-ask-timeout-advisor
description: Tells a PTC program's next request what its own deadline hid: that the human question it was waiting on was aborted, not answered. Discussion #8368: in PTC mode the model can only call `run_code`, and a program that asks through `tools.ask_user_question(...)` spends the program's wall-clock budget on the human wait — the runtime documents `timeoutMs` (default 120000 ms, capped by `maxTimeoutMs` at 600000) as "Default elapsed deadline, including nested tool and approval waits". When it expires, the nested call settles `UserQuestionError`/`ASK_ABORTED` and `run_code` reports `code run failed (timeout): execution deadline reached (120000ms)`, so the model sees a program failure and nothing that says the question is still unanswered — it steps forward as if the deadline were consent, where the ask tool's own contract says "A timeout is never approval". This plugin wraps the public `tools/execute` waterfall — the one seam that sees the nested sub-dispatches a program makes, because they run through the same registry pipeline — keeps an aborted ask against its call tree (`rootCallId`), and when that tree's program settles as a deadline cut, attaches one user-role advisory to the program's own result: the question was aborted rather than answered, do not perform the action it was gating, ask it again as a direct tool call outside the program (its own measured control waited over four minutes), and otherwise stop. Every gate fails toward silence: only a configured program, only a code-and-wording deadline failure, only an ask tool, only an abort code, and the record is taken rather than read so a tree cannot be advised twice.
